title: Amazon's new Alexa Tablets drop the Fire branding but are more Android than ever
gist: Amazon dropped Fire branding for Alexa Tablets (8, 11, 12 Pro) that are now Google-certified Android devices with the Play Store, priced from $230 to $500 and shipping October 14, with Alexa Plus as the AI core. Whitwam argues the hardware is price-competitive against iPads but app optimization for Android tablets remains thin.

themes.theme: Amazon's pivot from Fire OS to full Android

insights.claim: Amazon has retired the Fire tablet brand in favor of Alexa Tablets, and the new devices are Google-certified Android with the Play Store and Google apps, ending 15 years of downplaying Android.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Amazon abandoning its walled Android fork signals that the ecosystem moat of its own app store was not worth sustaining in tablets.
insights.quote: The company’s new tablet lineup is a big change, though.

insights.claim: Amazon shut down its Appstore last year, which removed the rationale for Fire OS and paved the way for Google-integrated Android on tablets.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Closing the Appstore made the move to Google Play almost inevitable; watch for further Amazon platform consolidation.
insights.locator: However, Amazon shut down its app store last year

insights.claim: Amazon is moving its Fire Sticks in the opposite direction, away from Android to the custom Linux-based Vega OS, so tablets and TV devices now run on diverging software stacks.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Amazon is splitting its device OS strategy by form factor, using Android where apps matter and in-house Linux where it wants control.
insights.locator: This contrasts sharply with Amazon’s Fire Sticks

insights.claim: The Alexa Tablet 8 starts at $230 and the Tablet 11 at $330, both on the budget MediaTek 8189 processor with 16:10 displays, a step up from the last-gen Fire tablets but a price increase over them.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Entry-level price points moved up, so Amazon is trading some volume-leader pricing for a more capable product.

insights.claim: The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $500 with a MediaTek Dimensity 8400, 8GB RAM, 128GB storage and a 2800x1840 120 Hz display at 500 nits, with optional keyboard ($150), stylus ($90) and matte display ($50).
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: The 12 Pro is Amazon's first serious attempt at a productivity tablet with accessories, aimed above the traditional Fire price band.
insights.locator: Starting at $500, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro

insights.claim: The lineup is available for preorder and ships October 14, and Whitwam expects it to be among the most popular Android slates simply because of heavy promotion on Amazon.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Distribution through Amazon's own storefront gives these tablets a volume advantage regardless of spec rivalry.
insights.locator: By simply being heavily promoted on Amazon

themes.theme: Alexa Plus as the AI layer

insights.claim: Alexa Plus is the core software experience on the new tablets, with the Alexa wake word, screen-context answers and product recommendations, even though users can also run Gemini or other Android AI apps.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: The tablet is a shopping-oriented distribution channel for Amazon's AI assistant, competing with Gemini on the same hardware.
insights.locator: With access to Google apps and the Play Store

insights.claim: Whitwam notes the AI will naturally suggest buying things on Amazon when possible, framing the assistant as a commerce funnel.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Assistant-driven product recommendations are Amazon's monetization path for subsidized hardware.
insights.locator: Naturally, it will suggest you buy things

insights.claim: Apple's iPad Mini now starts at $600, the iPad Air at $750 and the base iPad at $450, so Amazon's $230-$500 tablets remain price-competitive in 2026.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Amazon holds a clear price gap below Apple's range, targeting value buyers rather than the premium tier.
insights.locator: Apple’s iPad Mini now starts at $600

insights.claim: Despite the Play Store upgrade, there are still few Android apps optimized for tablets despite Google's repeated promises, which limits the benefit of the move to full Android.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: App-ecosystem quality, not hardware, is the binding constraint on Android tablets versus iPad.
